_readme: Curated by hand (strategy A9, 2026-10-09). Rendered at /pipeline/ by Atlas_v2 (src/pages/pipeline.astro, synced by scripts/sync_data.py). Rules: no ranking of companies, no investment language, every status line has a source and a checked date; 'atlas_studies' lists only SIDs that exist in studies_baked.json. Two dates, never merged: 'edited' = last editorial change of this file; 'registry_checked' = last time every trial in 'registry' was re-read on ClinicalTrials.gov and every company page in 'sources' was re-read. 'registry' holds one entry per NCT id: status and dates as the registry states them, 'last_update' = the registry's own last-update-posted date (filled by check_pipeline_registry.py), 'checked' = when we read it. Re-check monthly, and weekly for any trial whose planned start has passed while it is still 'Not yet recruiting' (check_pipeline_registry.py flags these). 'watchlist' = named candidates that have not reached clinical or late preclinical development; they are listed, not graded.
intro: Drugs that act on mTOR and are in clinical or late preclinical development, with what the Atlas's own evidence says about the reason each one exists. The common thread is one problem: rapamycin and its relatives block mTORC1, but with long exposure they also block mTORC2, and in mice the insulin resistance rapamycin causes is traced to that second hit (LAM2012).

groups.title: Selective mTORC1 inhibitors
groups.note: Built to block mTORC1 without touching mTORC2.

items.name: AV078
items.kind: Selective mTORC1 inhibitor that reaches the brain
items.status: Phase 1 in healthy adults completed in February 2025 (89 participants); no results are posted in the registry. A placebo-controlled phase 2, RESTOR-1, in tuberous sclerosis complex with drug-resistant epilepsy is registered for 42 participants with a planned start of 1 September 2026. On 18 October 2026 the registry still listed it as not yet recruiting, with one site (London, Ontario). The planned start has passed: either the start has slipped or the record has not been updated, and we found no sponsor announcement either way. The company raised a $55 million Series B in December 2025 to fund that phase 2.
items.atlas_says: No study on AV078 is in the Atlas yet. The reason a brain-penetrant mTORC1 inhibitor is tried in tuberous sclerosis is covered: everolimus shrinks TSC brain and kidney tumours in randomised trials (FRA2013, BIS2013), while a 2026 trial found no clear benefit on cognition (SAX2026).

sources.title: Business Wire, 16 Dec 2025: Aeovian raises $55 million

items.watch: Planned start passed while still not yet recruiting; re-check weekly until the registry or the sponsor says what happened.

items.name: RMC-5552
items.kind: Bi-steric mTORC1-selective inhibitor (binds both the rapamycin site and the kinase site)
items.status: First-in-human dose-escalation trial in advanced solid tumours completed (58 enrolled). A separate phase 1 trial in recurrent glioblastoma was terminated after 7 participants, before its later cohorts opened, because the drug was no longer provided by the sponsor. AdisInsight lists no development reported as of May 2026. That means no new development has been reported, not that the company has formally ended the programme.
items.atlas_says: In the phase 1 trial (57 patients, no comparison arm) high blood sugar caused by treatment was uncommon (4%) and not dose-limiting (SCH2025). That fits the idea that sparing mTORC2 avoids metabolic side effects, but an uncontrolled trial cannot show it. The preclinical basis, its sister compound RMC-6272 in breast cancer models, is MEN2023.

items.name: TOR-101
items.kind: Selective mTORC1 inhibitor from a rapalog portfolio licensed from Novartis
items.status: Cambrian Bio lists TOR-101 as "Phase 1 Prepared" for healthspan and intrinsic capacity, and says its platform received up to $30.8 million from ARPA-H's PROSPR programme. No TOR-101 trial was found on ClinicalTrials.gov on 18 October 2026.
items.atlas_says: No study on TOR-101 is in the Atlas. The case for an mTORC1-only drug in ageing rests on mouse work: chronic rapamycin also disrupts mTORC2 and causes insulin resistance, while lowering mTORC1 alone extended lifespan in female mice without it (LAM2012).

items.name: DL001
items.kind: Rapamycin analogue about 40 times more selective for mTORC1 than rapamycin
items.status: Published in mice in 2019: inhibited mTORC1 without impairing glucose homeostasis and with reduced or no effects on lipid metabolism and the immune system. No clinical trial found.

groups.title: Approved rapalogs tested against ageing
groups.note: Sirolimus (rapamycin) and everolimus are approved drugs. These trials ask whether a dose or schedule exists that helps older people without the side effects.

items.name: Everolimus, EVERLAST
items.sponsor: University of Wisconsin-Madison, funded by the National Institute on Aging
items.kind: Rapalog (inhibits mTORC1; with long exposure also mTORC2)
items.status: 106 participants aged 55 to 80 with insulin resistance, 24 weeks of daily 0.5 mg or weekly 5 mg everolimus against placebo. Primary outcome: insulin sensitivity. Completed July 2026; no results posted yet. Until they are, this trial says nothing either way about whether everolimus helps.
items.atlas_says: The Atlas has no result yet. The daily-versus-weekly comparison follows mouse work in which intermittent rapamycin largely spared glucose control and the immune system while still inhibiting mTORC1 (ARR2015) and, started late in life, extended female lifespan (ARR2016).

items.name: Sirolimus and everolimus, RAP PAC
items.sponsor: University of Wisconsin-Madison, funded by the NIH and the National Institute on Aging
items.status: Dose-finding: 5, 10 or 15 mg once a week for 6 weeks in adults aged 55 to 89, measuring drug levels, mTOR signalling in blood and muscle, and side effects. Primary completion expected March 2027.
items.atlas_says: This is the trial behind the open question of which weekly dose inhibits mTORC1 in older people while sparing mTORC2. See the Atlas page on rapamycin for the human studies so far.

groups.title: Stopped or failed
groups.note: Kept here on purpose. A failure is information.

items.name: RTB101 (dactolisib, BEZ235)
items.kind: Described by the sponsor as a TORC1 inhibitor; chemically BEZ235, a catalytic PI3K/mTOR inhibitor
items.status: PROTECTOR 1 randomised 1,024 adults aged 65 and over to RTB101 10 mg or placebo daily for 16 weeks. It did not reduce clinically symptomatic respiratory illness, and development for that use stopped in November 2019.
items.atlas_says: The phase 2a with low-dose BEZ235 plus everolimus was associated with fewer infections (MAN2018). The phase 3 moved the antiviral-gene biomarker but not the clinical outcome (MAN2021). The Atlas uses it as the clearest case of a biomarker that did not become a benefit.

sources.title: resTORbio press release via BioSpace, 15 Nov 2019

items.name: SPN-820 (NV-5138)
items.kind: The opposite direction: an mTORC1 activator, binding Sestrin2, developed for depression
items.status: In about 250 adults with treatment-resistant depression, 4 weeks of SPN-820 did not beat placebo on the MADRS depression scale (change -12.3 versus -11.9). Announced February 2025.
items.atlas_says: No clinical study of NV-5138 is in the Atlas. It appears only as a laboratory tool for switching mTORC1 on (RAUCH2026).

approved_note: Already approved and not listed above: sirolimus (transplant rejection, lymphangioleiomyomatosis), everolimus (several cancers, tuberous sclerosis tumours and seizures, transplant), temsirolimus (kidney cancer) and nab-sirolimus (PEComa). See the drug pages in the Atlas.
reading_note: Two distinctions hold everywhere on this page. A trial that is completed with no results posted is not a negative trial: it has simply not reported. And a trial that stopped is not the same as a programme that stopped; where we say no development is reported, that is what the source says, not proof that the company has ended the work.

NCT07680322.dates: planned start 1 Sep 2026, primary completion Sep 2027

NCT05557292.dates: closed to accrual before cohorts B and C opened

watchlist.note: Named candidates a sponsor has announced but that have not reached clinical or late preclinical development. Listed so they can be followed, not graded; they move up into the sections above once a trial is registered or preclinical data are published.

items.name: TOR-103
items.status: Listed by Cambrian Bio as a "Candidate" for respiratory tract infections and for oncology. No trial found on ClinicalTrials.gov and no study in the Atlas.
